reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G3-NA-Q3-Harden (mat_g3_na_q3_2), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sample problems directly address all multiplication objectives stated in the competency text. The packet includes 2-digit by 1-digit multiplication with regrouping (e.g., "What is 41 × 6?" and "69 × 3 = ___"), 3-digit by 1-digit multiplication without regrouping (e.g., "What is 401 × 2?" and "101 × 5 = ___") and with regrouping (e.g., "What is 104 × 7?"), as well as multiplications of 2- to 4-digit numbers by numbers whose leading digit is the only non-zero digit (e.g., "22 × 30 = ___" and "1000 × 10 = ___"). All products remain within the 10 000 limit.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The problem set spans the full range of required sub-cases: 2-digit and 3-digit multiplicands multiplied by 1-digit multipliers, both regrouped and non-regrouped, alongside 2-digit to 4-digit multiplicands multiplied by multiples of 10/100 (such as "What is 10 × 80?", "What is 33 × 300?", and "1000 × 10 = ___"). Both procedural computation and conceptual error checking are thoroughly tested.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The cognitive load is tailored accurately to Grade 3 Quarter 3 learners. Syntax is clear, direct, and concise (e.g., "What is 12 × 60?" and "11 × 60 = 600. True or False?"). The error detection items (e.g., "Grace solved: "48 × 4 = ___". Grace says the missing number is 44. Is Grace correct?) assess conceptual reasoning without unnecessary reading friction.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The samples demonstrate diverse assessment formats including multiple-choice ("What is 41 × 6?"), cloze fill-in-the-blank ("22 × 30 = ___"), true/false ("11 × 60 = 600. True or False?"), and error detection (Rico solved: "1000 × 10 = ___". Rico says the missing number is 10000. Is Rico correct?), ensuring students are tested on both calculation fluency and reasoning.

competency_alignment.rationale: All generated items adhere strictly to the competency boundaries. No out-of-scope multiplication concepts (such as 2-digit by general 2-digit numbers with multiple non-zero digits) are present. Every problem matches either a 1-digit multiplier or a multiplier with only a leading non-zero digit, adhering exactly to the MATATAG scope.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical scale across all items complies strictly with the specified limit of products up to 10 000. Problems scale naturally from small 2-digit multiplications resulting in products in the hundreds (e.g., "Grace solved: "48 × 4 = ___". Grace says the missing number is 44. Is Grace correct?" with product 192) up to the upper bound of 10 000 (e.g., "What is 33 × 300?" yielding 9900, and "1000 × 10 = ___" yielding 10000).
